before.title: 48-Volt Integrated Starter-Generator / DC-DC Converter Failure Causing Warning Messages, Limp Mode, or No Restart
before.description: Owners of six-cylinder CLS 450 models have reported failures in the 48V mild-hybrid system, including the integrated starter-generator, 48V battery support components, or DC-DC converter. Symptoms include 'Stop Vehicle Leave Engine Running,' multiple warning lights, loss of charging support, disabled start/stop, reduced power, and in some cases inability to restart after shutting the car off. This issue is well documented across Mercedes models using the M256/48V architecture and appears in owner complaints and service literature.
before.solution: Perform a full scan of both 12V and 48V systems with Mercedes-capable diagnostics, checking charging voltage, converter operation, and fault memory in the powertrain and energy management modules. Repairs vary by root cause but commonly involve replacing the DC-DC converter, 48V battery, wiring, or the integrated starter-generator assembly, followed by software updates and battery registration/adaptation. Because the system is safety-critical and high-voltage relative to standard 12V systems, diagnosis is best handled by a Mercedes specialist or dealer.
symptoms: stop vehicle leave engine running message

communityRecommendations.content: Do not keep driving on repeated 48V warnings; low converter output can cascade into 12V undervoltage faults and strand the car.
Use a Mercedes-capable scan tool that can read 48V and energy management modules, not just generic OBD-II.

proposal.title: 48-Volt Integrated Starter-Generator / DC-DC Converter Failure Causing Warning Messages, Limp Mode, or No Restart
proposal.description: XENTRY LI54.10-P-069698 directly includes model series 257 with code B01, but it describes several distinct 48V conditions: software-related intermittent or permanent no-starts, a 48V-system short, battery disconnection after an abnormality, connector or cable faults and cause-specific component testing. It does not establish one recurring integrated-starter-generator/DC-DC hardware failure across every 2019-2024 CLS 450 and AMG CLS 53 or validate the frozen generic fault-code list.
proposal.solution: Preserve the exact warning sequence and complete 12V/48V fault data, identify the applicable cause in LI54.10-P-069698 and complete the specified software, cable, connection and component tests before replacement. Do not buy an ISG, DC/DC converter, 48V battery or cable from this page; the failed component and VIN-level fitment are not established.
symptoms: exact 48V warning and no-start sequence recorded
software, cables and connections checked before hardware replacement

before.title: Front Brake Squeal and Premature Rotor/Pads Wear on AMG-Line and AMG Variants
before.description: Owners of CLS models with larger sport brake packages, especially CLS 450 AMG Line and AMG CLS 53, frequently report persistent front brake squeal, groan at low speeds, and faster-than-expected pad/rotor wear. In many cases the brakes still function normally, but noise and rotor scoring lead to repeated dealer visits. This is a common real-world complaint on Mercedes performance-oriented brake setups using aggressive pad compounds.
before.solution: Inspect pad thickness, rotor runout, rotor surface condition, and caliper slide/piston operation. Mercedes dealers often apply updated pad shims, anti-squeal compound, bedding procedures, or replace pads/rotors if glazing or scoring is present. Using OE-spec friction materials and proper bedding is important; cheap aftermarket pads often worsen noise or dust.

communityRecommendations.content: If the brakes squeal after recent service, ask whether the pads were properly bedded and whether anti-squeal paste/shims were installed.
Owners wanting less dust/noise should stick with reputable OE-equivalent pads rather than the cheapest aftermarket options.

proposal.title: Front Brake Squeal and Premature Rotor/Pads Wear on AMG-Line and AMG Variants
proposal.description: Mercedes AMG brake communications describe service-brake noise and squeal as frictional vibration that can vary with speed, brake pressure, driving style, temperature and humidity. They direct technicians to reproduce the complaint and inspect wear or damage. They do not establish premature rotor/pad wear across 2019-2024 CLS 450 AMG Line and AMG CLS 53 vehicles or prove updated shims, anti-squeal compound and pad/rotor replacement as universal remedies.
proposal.solution: Reproduce the noise safely, identify the axle and brake package, measure pad thickness, rotor thickness and runout, and inspect surfaces, hardware and caliper movement using the VIN-specific procedure. Do not buy pads, rotors, shims or calipers from this page; measured condition and exact fitment are unresolved.
symptoms: pad and rotor measurements documented before parts selection

before.title: MBUX / Instrument Cluster Software Freezes, Black Screens, and Backup Camera Malfunctions
before.description: Current-generation CLS models use the widescreen MBUX infotainment and digital cluster system, and owners have reported intermittent screen blackouts, frozen displays, reboot loops, inoperative audio/navigation, and backup camera image failures. Mercedes has issued multiple software updates and service guidance for MBUX-related glitches across this platform. While often software-related, some cases involve display, camera, or control unit replacement when updates do not resolve the issue.
before.solution: Check for stored communication and infotainment faults, verify software level, and apply the latest Mercedes head-unit/instrument cluster updates. If the concern includes a blank reverse camera or persistent black screen, inspect LVDS/video connections, camera module operation, and power/ground integrity before replacing hardware. Battery voltage should also be tested because low system voltage can trigger false MBUX faults.
symptoms: touchpad or steering wheel controls unresponsive

communityRecommendations.content: Ask the dealer to document current software versions before approving expensive hardware replacement; many cases are fixed by programming.
If the backup camera fails intermittently, record a video of the symptom because it often disappears before service appointments.

before.title: Panoramic Sunroof Creaking, Popping, or Binding from Glass/Frame Adjustment and Seal Friction
before.description: A recurring owner complaint on the C257 CLS is noise from the panoramic roof area, especially over driveways, uneven pavement, or in hot/cold weather. The problem is usually not shattered glass but creaking or popping caused by seal friction, roof panel adjustment, or frame movement. Mercedes service departments commonly address it with lubrication, seal treatment, and roof alignment procedures, though some cars need repeat visits.
before.solution: Road-test the vehicle over low-speed body-twist conditions to isolate the roof from interior trim noises. Clean and condition the roof seals, inspect tracks and panel alignment, and perform factory adjustment procedures for the glass and frame if needed. If noise persists, inspect for loose fasteners or worn guide components in the roof cassette.

communityRecommendations.content: Many owners report temporary improvement after cleaning and treating the roof seals with a Mercedes-approved rubber care product.
Reproduce the noise with the shade open and closed to help separate glass/seal noise from headliner trim rattles.

before.title: 7G-Tronic Transmission Valve Body Failure
before.description: The 722.9 7G-Tronic automatic transmission in CLS models suffers from valve body conductor plate failures. The electronic conductor plate controls shift solenoids and develops internal short circuits or loses communication, causing harsh shifting, getting stuck in limp mode, or refusing to shift out of park. This is one of the most common transmission failures on Mercedes vehicles of this era.
before.solution: Replace the valve body conductor plate (also called the TCU sleeve or electrical connector plate). The valve body itself may also need replacement if the solenoids are worn. Fluid and filter change should be performed simultaneously with Mercedes-approved ATF.
symptoms: Transmission stuck in limp mode (3rd gear only)
Failure to shift out of park intermittently

before.title: AIRMATIC Air Suspension Strut Failure
before.description: The optional AIRMATIC air suspension on the C218 CLS-Class develops air leaks in the front struts and rear air springs. The rubber bladders crack from age and heat exposure, causing the vehicle to sag overnight. The compressor then overworks trying to maintain ride height, leading to compressor burnout as a secondary failure.
before.solution: Replace the leaking air strut or air spring. Arnott and Bilstein offer quality aftermarket alternatives at significant savings over OEM. Replace all four if budget allows, as they age at similar rates. Inspect the compressor relay and valve block.
symptoms: Vehicle sitting low on one corner after parking

before.title: Crankshaft Position Sensor Failure
before.description: The crankshaft position sensor on M276 and M278 engines in the CLS fails without warning, causing an immediate engine stall and no-start condition. The sensor is located in a heat-exposed area near the bellhousing, and thermal cycling degrades the sensor over time. This is a roadside breakdown item that leaves the vehicle completely inoperable.
before.solution: Replace the crankshaft position sensor. This is a relatively inexpensive part ($50-100) but can be labor-intensive to access depending on the engine variant. Carry a spare sensor in the trunk if the vehicle is high-mileage. Use only OEM Bosch sensors for reliability.
symptoms: Check engine light with crank sensor codes
Intermittent engine cutting out at idle

before.title: LED Headlight Ballast and Control Module Failure
before.description: The Multibeam LED headlight system on the C218 CLS-Class experiences ballast and LED driver module failures. Individual LED segments within the headlight assembly stop functioning, and the control module throws faults. Replacement of individual LED elements is not possible — the entire headlight assembly must be replaced, making this an expensive repair.
before.solution: Replace the failed headlight assembly or have a specialist repair the LED driver board if available. Mercedes dealers require full headlight replacement. Some independent shops can repair the LED driver board at a fraction of the cost. Check for updated part numbers that address the failure.
symptoms: One or more LED segments not illuminating

before.title: M272 Balance Shaft Gear Wear and Failure
before.description: The M272 V6 and M273 V8 engines in early CLS models suffer from a well-documented balance shaft gear failure where the idler gear sprocket wears prematurely due to a manufacturing defect. The worn gear produces a rattling noise on startup and can eventually cause engine timing issues and catastrophic damage if the gear teeth strip completely.
before.solution: Replace the balance shaft gear, idler gear, and associated chain with the updated Mercedes parts (revised sprocket material). This is a significant repair requiring partial engine disassembly. If caught early before timing is affected, the repair prevents further engine damage.
symptoms: Rattling or chattering noise on cold start
Check engine light with timing codes
Rough idle that worsens over time
